title: ReviewBench: An open benchmark for AI code review
key_facts: GitHub, with Microsoft, built ReviewBench, an offline benchmark for AI code review agents; the post says it is available to use today and that a research preview version is on the ReviewBench website, where people can compare code review agents and submit their own.

The benchmark holds 219 public pull requests from 187 public open source licensed repositories in 19 languages; GitHub analysed 103.9 million pull requests so that language and repository-size mix matches GitHub overall, and it weights pull-request size toward larger, multi-file changes.

Every finding is labelled for severity and category; ReviewBench reports six metrics in two families (known issues and newly discovered ones), with grounded recall as the headline cross-system comparison, and users can weight precision against recall.

Before release, senior engineers who had not helped build the dataset re-labelled every ground-truth finding from scratch; their true/false-positive judgments agreed with ReviewBench 96.6% of the time. GitHub says it versions the dataset, judge and matcher and publishes the validation method and known threats to validity.
GitHub says it uses ReviewBench to evaluate its own Copilot code review (CCR) and that offline changes have consistently pointed the same way as later production results.

Example given: a lite-tier multi-model ensemble review. ReviewBench predicted higher precision, recall and comment volume with lower cost per review; the online A/B test showed addressed rate (precision) +8.0%, recall +13.6%, comment volume +61% and cost per review -8.0%, all relative to the production control.
Severity check given: ReviewBench predicted a 227% increase in critical comments; the online figure was 262%.
quote_evidence: We built ReviewBench, a new code review offline benchmark, to address that gap, and it is available for you to use today.

why_it_matters_hint: Teams that build or choose AI code reviewers get a public yardstick, and GitHub says it already predicts how changes to its own Copilot code review perform with real users.
